# Trapezium

> A data table library for React, Vue, Svelte and plain JavaScript. Zero-config columns with type
> inference, multi-column sorting, per-column filters, global search, an optional search box in each
> column header, four pagination modes, selection, custom renderers, SSR, URL state and CSS-variable
> theming. No runtime dependencies.

Packages: @trapezium/react, @trapezium/vue, @trapezium/svelte, @trapezium/vanilla, @trapezium/core
Licence: MIT. Repository: https://github.com/Gregaly/trapezium

## Minimal usage

    import { Table } from "@trapezium/react"
    import "@trapezium/react/styles.css"

    <Table data={rows} />

Columns, headers, types, alignment, formatting, sorting, search and pagination are all inferred from
the data. Add configuration only to override a default.

## Common usage

    <Table
      data={rows}
      getRowId={(row) => row.id}
      search
      selection
      onSelectionChange={(ids, rows) => {}}
      export
      pagination={{ mode: "pages", pageSize: 25 }}
      format={{ locale: "en-AU", timeZone: "Australia/Sydney", currency: "AUD" }}
      columns={[
        { key: "reference", header: "Invoice", pin: "start" },
        { key: "customer.name", header: "Customer" },
        { key: "amount", type: "currency", filter: "range" },
        { key: "status", type: "badge", formatOptions: { options: STATUSES } },
        { key: "due_date", type: "date" },
        { key: "actions", header: "", sortable: false, render: ({ row }) => <Menu id={row.id} /> },
      ]}
    />

## Table props

data · columns · getRowId(row, index) · state · defaultState · onStateChange(state) · server ·
total · loading · error · search · filters · headerSearch · sortable · resizable · reorderable ·
columnMenu ·
columnControl · pagination · selection · onSelectionChange(ids, rows) · export · density ·
densityControl · responsive("scroll"|"cards") · stickyHeader · maxHeight ·
rowHeight("fixed"|"auto"|number) · types · format ·
rowHref(row) · onRowClick(row, event) · onRowContextMenu(row, event, info) · rowClassName(row, index, info) · detail · getParentId(row) ·
pinnedRows({ top, bottom }) · rowReorder({ canDrag, onReorder }) ·
cellNavigation ·
onCellEdit(edit) · editTrigger("click"|"doubleClick") · emptyState · emptyMessage ·
toolbar · appendRow · footer · buildHref(state) · linkComponent (React) · onNavigate(href, event) ·
className · classNames ·
unstyled · theme("light"|"dark") · id · aria-label · caption

Booleans default to sensible: filters, sortable, resizable, reorderable, columnMenu, columnControl
and stickyHeader are on; search, headerSearch, selection, export, densityControl are off until
asked for.

## Sorting

Click a header: ascending, descending, off. Shift-click a second header to sort by it within the
first; each sorted header then shows its level (1, 2, 3). A shift-click on a sorted header reverses
that level in place, and a third removes it. A plain click replaces the whole sort. Without a shift
key: "Then sort ascending" / "Then sort descending" in a column's menu, once another column is
sorted. While a sort is applied a reset button leads the toolbar's controls and clears it; with
`buildHref` it is a link. state.sort is an ordered array of { key, direction }.

    sortable                                   // default: true, multi-column, with the reset
    sortable={false}                           // no sorting
    sortable={{ multiple: false }}             // one column at a time (a backend that orders by one)
    sortable={{ reset: false }}                // no reset control
    sortable={{ reset: [{ key: "created_at", direction: "desc" }] }}
                                               // the table rests in this order: the reset returns
                                               // to it and is hidden while the table is in it

The reset is a toolbar control: a table with no toolbar controls at all (no search, columnControl
false, no export) shows none. Per column: sortable:false, compare(a, b). Empty values sort last in
both directions. In code: toggleSort(state, key, additive?) · addSort(state, key, direction) ·
removeSort(state, key) · resetSort(state, to?) · clearSort(state).

rowHeight: "fixed" (default) is one line a cell with an ellipsis. "auto" and a number both let every
cell wrap, whatever a cell renderer put there — it is CSS only, because the table is a real <table>
in normal flow, so there is no measuring pass, no ResizeObserver and no layout shift on the server.
They differ only in where the height comes from: "auto" grows each row to its tallest cell with
--tpz-row-height as the floor, a number gives them all that height and ends what will not fit in an
ellipsis, on however many lines the height allows (the count is worked out in CSS, nothing is
measured). Only "fixed" truncates to one line. Wrapped rows align to the top, the selection checkbox centred on the first
line of text; fixed and exact rows stay centred. The header has its own --tpz-header-height and does not follow rowHeight; density
moves both. Per column: wrap:false keeps one line whichever wrapping mode is on, wrap:true wraps,
wrap:3 wraps and stops after three lines.

Append pagination ("loadMore", "infinite") keeps every page loaded so far on screen and renders only
the rows it just added: the rows already there are not rebuilt, their cell renderers are not re-run,
and the scroll position is not disturbed. That is what makes rowHeight:"auto" affordable on a long
infinite list.

## Performance (client mode, 100,000 rows, 26 columns, Node, ms)

sort by text ~97 · set filter ~29 · search keystroke ~33–39 once each row's search text is built
(built in idle time automatically when the table has a search box and ≥2,000 rows; cold first
keystroke ~0.7–1.2 s otherwise) · page turn / selection / active-cell move / detail toggle ~0.01
(each pipeline stage is remembered until its inputs change: rows by identity — replace the array
to change data — columns, types, format, and that stage's part of the state). Headless:
getRows({ ..., cache: createPipelineCache() }), warmSearch(rows, columns, types, format, from,
budgetMs), warmSearchWhenIdle(...). Append pagination keeps the DOM bounded to loaded rows; past
~10,000 loaded rows the browser's cost per appended page grows (268 ms at 20,000 rows) — use
mode "pages" for very long lists. Numbers and the windowed-append proposal: docs/performance.md.

## Export

export={{ filename, scope: "matching" | "page", clipboard, fetchRows(state), onExport(state, rows) }}

Default scope is "matching": every row the filters and search leave, in the current sort order and
column arrangement, not the page on screen. Numbers, dates and currency are written as values a
spreadsheet can add up rather than as the formatted text. A selection, if any, wins for the
clipboard copy.

## Column definition

key (required, supports dotted paths and synthetic ids) · header · description · type · accessor(row) ·
format(ctx)=>string · formatOptions · render(ctx)=>node · renderHeader(ctx)=>node ·
renderHeaderControls(ctx)=>node · sortable ·
compare(a,b) · searchable · filter · headerSearch · align · width (held exactly) · minWidth ·
maxWidth (caps cells too) · grow(number: share of spare width; others keep to content) ·
pin("start"|"end"|{ side, below?, above? }: frozen only under/over that table width, by a CSS
container query, so SSR matches; stays in place in the order) ·
hidden · resizable · reorderable · wrap(boolean|number) · mono · icon · exportable · exportValue(ctx) · className ·
headerClassName · meta · editable(boolean|(row)=>boolean) · renderEditor(ctx) · parse(value, row) ·
validate(value, row)

`format` replaces the cell text and keeps sorting/filtering on the raw value.
`render` replaces the cell markup. CellContext = { value, row, rowIndex, rowId, column, text, format }.
`renderHeader({ column, sort })` replaces the header's TEXT only; the icon/magnifier, sort control
(arrow, level), menu and resize handle stay and work. It renders inside the sort button, so return
phrasing content (text/icons/badges, no links or buttons); the button keeps `header` as its
accessible name. Rendered on the server in every adapter (Vue: may return a VNode).
`renderHeaderControls({ column, sort })` puts CONTROLS in the header (a search box, a filter button):
after the sort button, before the menu, outside the sort button, so links/buttons/inputs are fine.
They take the header's spare width. A click or press in them never sorts or drags the column.
React and Vue keep them in place across state changes (an input keeps focus and text); plain JS and
Svelte: return the SAME node each time to keep it ("" leaves the slot empty). Rendered on the
server. Hidden with the header row in the cards layout — put a control phones need in the toolbar.
`description: "…"` shows a tooltip on header hover/focus (Escape hides it) and links the text with
aria-describedby; a dotted underline marks described headers.

## Cell renderers

A row of one line is exactly --tpz-row-height at every density (28 / 32 / 40px at compact / normal /
relaxed), with rowHeight "fixed" or "auto", whatever the cells hold. Every built-in type keeps to
that. A `render` keeps to it by following four rules:

- Inherit the font size. No fixed text sizes; size icons in em (`width: 1em; height: 1em`).
- Never scroll: no `overflow: auto` or `overflow: scroll` inside a cell.
- No padding or margin above the first line, so it lines up with the other columns' first line.
- Stay on one line unless the row is meant to grow. Anything taller than one line (a button, a
  pill, an avatar) is at most `var(--tpz-text-cell-leading)` tall, with `vertical-align: top`.

Variables a renderer can use, at compact / normal / relaxed:

    --tpz-text-cell            11px / 11px / 12px   the cell's font size (inherited already)
    --tpz-text-cell-leading    16px / 16px / 16px   one line; anything inline should fit in it
    --tpz-row-height           28px / 32px / 40px   the whole row, including the cell's 1px bottom border
    --tpz-cell-padding-y        5px /  6px /  6px   top and bottom padding of a cell, but only under
                                                    rowHeight "auto" or a number, or wrap:true;
                                                    a "fixed" row has none and centres its content
    --tpz-cell-content-height  the height inside the cell: --tpz-row-height less the 1px border, and
                               less both paddings where the cell is padded.
                               fixed: 27px / 31px / 39px.  auto: 17px / 19px / 27px.
                               rowHeight={N}: N − 1 − 2 × --tpz-cell-padding-y.

To fill a cell use `height: var(--tpz-cell-content-height)`, never `height: var(--tpz-row-height)`,
which is a pixel taller than the cell has and grows the row. --tpz-cell-content-height is set on
`.tpz-td`, so it only exists inside a cell. With a number for rowHeight the row is the number and
the same variables apply. Inside a cell `.tpz-badge` is 16px tall at the cell's text size less 1px
(10 / 10 / 11px), and `.tpz-btn` is 16px tall at the cell's text size, so both are safe to use in a
renderer; outside a cell they keep their interface sizes.

    .row-action {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      height: var(--tpz-text-cell-leading);   /* one line */
      padding: 0 0.5rem;                      /* nothing above the line */
      font: inherit;                          /* the cell's size */
      line-height: 1;
      vertical-align: top;                    /* fills the line instead of poking out of it */
    }

## Types

text longText number currency percent boolean date datetime time relativeTime select badge tags
email url phone image id code address file json

Snake_case aliases accepted (long_text, multi_select→tags, timestamptz→datetime, money→currency,
uuid→id, jsonb→json, int8→number).

Custom type:

    defineType({ name: "rating", align: "end", format: (v) => "*".repeat(Number(v)),
                 normalise: (v) => Number(v), filter: "range" })
    <Table types={{ rating }} columns={[{ key: "stars", type: "rating" }]} />

`normalise` reduces a value to something orderable; sorting and filtering both use it.

Inference: the key first (status/state → badge, *_id → id, email, *_url, avatar → image, …), then
the values. A string column with ≥20 rows and ≤6 distinct values becomes a badge — except in a
`server` table, where the rows are one page and that guess would change as the user paged or
filtered, so the column is text. Set `type: "badge"` to have badges there.

## Filters

Kinds: text, set (checkbox list of values present in the data), range, date, boolean, none.
Operators: eq ne contains notContains startsWith endsWith gt gte lt lte between in notIn empty notEmpty.
A date filter written as a day matches the whole day. Empty cells satisfy no comparison. 0 and false
are not empty. A boolean filter's value is the word "true" or "false" and is read as that word.
Each value is typed into the box that can hold it (filterInputType): text for the text and list
operators, a date picker for date kinds, a number box for range kinds, a time picker for a time
column. "Is between" with one end filled is "at least" / "at most" (rangeFilter). The text operators (contains, notContains, startsWith, endsWith) match what a cell
SHOWS as well as what it stores, for every type: contains "Aug" finds a date, contains "1,2" finds
$1,240.00, contains "Professional" finds a select stored as "pro". Case, accents and the kind of
space are ignored. The other operators compare values through the column's type.

## Header search (optional, off by default)

    <Table data={rows} headerSearch />                       // every column that can be filtered
    <Table data={rows} headerSearch={{ debounce: 300 }} />   // wait 300ms after a keystroke (default 150)
    columns={[{ key: "name", headerSearch: true }]}          // one column only
    columns={[{ key: "notes", headerSearch: false }]}        // opt one column out

A magnifier replaces the column's type icon while its header is hovered or focused; clicking it turns
the header into a text box (laid over the header, so no column changes width). Typing filters that
column: it sets { key, operator: "contains", value } in state.filters — the same filter the column
menu edits — so it shows as a chip, is in the URL, reaches onStateChange, narrows exports and
replaces any other filter on that column. Enter applies and closes; Escape clears, then closes;
clicking away keeps what was typed. Works for every type by the text the cells show (see Filters).
image and json columns get none unless the column sets headerSearch:true, and nor does a column
with no heading (header: ""). `filters={false}` turns it off everywhere. A column's own `format` function is not consulted, only its type's formatting.
In code: setColumnSearch(state, key, text) ("" removes it) · columnSearchText(state, key).
In server mode the filter is sent like any other; answer `contains` on a formatted column with
matchesFilter(value, filter, defaultTypeRegistry.get(type), format) using the table's own format, or
enable headerSearch only on text columns.

## Columns: moving and removing

Drag a header sideways to move it (a line shows the landing edge), drag a row in the column list, or
use "Move left"/"Move right" in the column panel. Drag a header out of the table to remove it, with a
puff of smoke; the last visible column refuses. All of it lands in state.order / state.hidden.
Disable with reorderable={false} on the table or a column. Pinned columns are not draggable.

## Selection

selection · selection="single" · selection={{ mode, isSelectable(row, index), onChange(ids, rows),
selectAll: "page" | "matching", dragSelect: boolean }}
A row `isSelectable` refuses gets a disabled checkbox; the header checkbox and shift-click ranges skip
it. Ids come from getRowId (row.id, then row.uuid, then the index). The header selects the page on
screen by default; selectAll: "matching" makes it select every row the filters/search leave on every
page (label "Select all N matching rows"; in server mode it fetches them with server.all(state),
else selects the page and warns). dragSelect: true selects the rows a press sweeps across (5px
threshold so a click stays a click; the ending click is swallowed; ignores links/buttons/inputs/the
drag handle/an editing cell; auto-scrolls at the edges; Shift extends from the last chosen row,
otherwise the sweep replaces the selection; mouse/pen only). Shift+ArrowUp/Down from a row checkbox
(or any cell with cellNavigation) extends a range from an anchor (shrinks on the way back), and
Escape clears the selection (editors and menus keep their own Escape). In code: rangeSelection(base,
ids, anchor, target), startDragSelect. Same forms in every adapter.

## Detail rows (master/detail)

    detail={{ render: ({ row, rowId, rowIndex, collapse }) => node,
              canExpand: (row) => boolean,   // default: every row
              keepMounted: false,            // keep a closed detail mounted (hidden) so it does not refetch
              toggleOnRowClick: false }}     // a click anywhere on the row toggles it too

An expander column (a chevron button per row with aria-expanded/aria-controls, and one in the
header for every row on the page) leads the table. Any number of rows open at once. Open rows are
state.expanded: string[] (row ids) — controlled, saved, and URL-serialisable when asked for:
stateToQueryString(state, { include: [...DEFAULT_URL_KEYS, "expanded"] }) writes `open=id1,id2`.
The server renders open rows open. A detail row spans every column, is as tall as its content
(normal flow, nothing measured), keeps its content to the frame's width, and is never counted,
paged, sorted, selected or exported; it follows its row through sorting and paging. Append
pagination leaves open details alone. In cards layout it opens under the card. keepMounted mounts
on first open, then hides on close. In code: toggleExpanded(state, id) · setExpanded(state, ids,
open) · collapseAll(state) · isExpanded(state, id). Vue: render may return a VNode; plain JS and
Svelte: a node or a string. Pass `id` when a page has several tables with detail rows.

## Child rows (one level)

    <Table data={flatRows} getParentId={(row) => row.order_id /* or null */} />

Rows are given flat; a row whose parent id is in data is drawn directly under it, indented, and the
parent's leading cell gets a toggle (aria-expanded) that folds its children: state.collapsed:
string[] (parent ids; children shown unless named). Sorting orders parents, and children among
themselves. Filters/search test each row on its own: a parent is shown if it matches OR any child
matches (then as context: data-context="true", muted); a parent matching with no matching child is
shown alone; a child is shown if it matches. Paging and totals count parents (families): a parent
and its children are never split across pages. Folding is presentation only: folded children are
still matched and exported. Children are rows: selectable, editable, exportable (export keeps them
under their parent). Missing parent → shown as its own row (server mode: send whole families).
Deeper chains go under the top ancestor; loops stand alone. Server mode: groups the page given, no
filtering/sorting/paging. rowClassName(row, index, info) with info = { depth: 0|1, parentId,
childCount, context }; attributes data-depth="1", data-parent, data-context; .tpz-tree slot and
.tpz-tree-toggle in the leading cell. With cellNavigation the table is role="treegrid" with
aria-level/aria-expanded on rows. URL: include "collapsed" → fold=. In code: toggleCollapsed,
setCollapsed, isCollapsed, parentIdsWithChildren(rows, getParentId) (for collapse all). Not
grouping, not aggregation, not multi-level trees.

## Pinned rows

    pinnedRows={{ top: [newEntryRow], bottom: [totalsRow] }}

Rows outside data, in their own <tbody data-pinned="top|bottom">, drawn through the same columns,
renderers, formatting and editors, and sticky while the body scrolls (top ones under the sticky
header). Never filtered, searched, sorted, paged, counted, selected (no checkbox) or exported.
Editable: onCellEdit gets pinned: "top"|"bottom" (a "new entry" row = handle the edit by adding a
row). Keyboard: part of the grid (ArrowUp from the first body row reaches the pinned top row).
Ids: row.id / getRowId, else "top-0", "bottom-0". Empty cells are blank. Offsets: a row height each
on the server, measured in the browser. Style: --tpz-pinned-bg.

## Row reorder (drag)

    rowReorder={{ canDrag: (row) => !row.locked,
                  onReorder: ({ rowId, row, afterId, beforeId, parentId }) => save() /* may return a Promise */ }}
    // reorder an array: setRows((rs) => applyRowMove(rs, rs.map((r) => r.id), move))

A drag-handle column (".tpz-drag-handle", slot dragCell) leads the table. Pointer drag (not HTML5
DnD) with a drop line (data-drop="before"|"after") and auto-scroll near the scroll area's (or the
window's) edges; Escape cancels. Keyboard: Alt+ArrowUp/Down on the handle — or on any cell with
cellNavigation — moves one place, focus stays, and a live region announces "Moved to position N of
M". afterId = the row it now follows (null if first), beforeId = the row it now precedes (null if
last), counted among all matching rows in client mode (not just the page), the page in server mode.
Only offered while unsorted (handles aria-disabled under a sort). Children move among siblings only
(parentId set); a parent moves with its children. Pinned rows don't move. canDrag false → no
handle. The table never mutates data; a returned Promise shows the new order until it settles
(reverts on rejection). Touch: long-press the handle to drag; scrolling is never blocked before
that. In code: moveRowTo, stepRow, applyRowMove, canReorderRows, startRowDrag.

## Context menu

    onRowContextMenu={(row, event, { rowId, columnKey, column, text, rowText, pinned }) => {
      event.preventDefault()          // the browser's menu opens too unless you prevent it
      openMyMenu(event.clientX, event.clientY)
    }}

columnKey/column: the cell under the pointer (null over the checkbox/expander/handle columns).
text: what that cell shows (cellDisplayText; "" for empty). rowText: the row exactly as the table's
"Copy to clipboard" writes it (tab-separated export values, no header) — use for "Copy row".
cellDisplayText(row, column, { types, format }) and toDelimitedText are exported. Vue:
@row-context-menu.

onRowClick (and toggleOnRowClick) ignore clicks on controls inside the row: a[href], button,
input, select, textarea, label, [role=menu*], [role=button] and the like, or anything with
data-tpz-interactive. isInteractiveTarget(target, row) is exported.

## Keyboard cell navigation (opt-in; on automatically when a column is editable)

    <Table data={rows} cellNavigation />

The table becomes role="grid" with one tab stop (the active cell, tabindex=0). Arrows move one cell
(no wrapping), Home/End to the row's ends, Ctrl/Cmd+Home/End to the page's corners, PageUp/PageDown
by a screenful. Enter/F2 opens an editable cell's editor, else focuses the cell's link/button;
Escape returns to the cell. Space/Enter work the selection checkbox and expander from their cells.
Clicking a cell makes it active. Focus ring: --tpz-focus-ring. The active cell is state.focus:
{ rowId, key?, align?: "start"|"center"|"end"|"nearest" } | null — so it is declarative: set it
(focusCell(state, rowId, key?, align?)) from a banner and the table brings the row onto its page
(client mode; state.page follows and onStateChange reports it), scrolls it into view, highlights the
row (data-focused="true", --tpz-focused) and, with cellNavigation, focuses the cell (the row's first
cell when key is omitted). Not focused on the first render (only scrolled). Same value again does
nothing; clearFocus(state) first. Server mode: set page yourself. URL: include "focus" → at=rowId:key.
There is no imperative ref API; this is the scrollToRow/focusCell equivalent. Rows carry data-row-id.

## Inline editing

    columns={[{ key: "qty", type: "number", editable: true,
                parse: (v, row) => v, validate: (v, row) => v >= 0 || "Must be zero or more" },
              { key: "price", type: "currency", editable: (row) => !row.invoiced },
              { key: "status", formatOptions: { options: STATUSES }, editable: true },
              { key: "owner", editable: true,
                renderEditor: ({ value, initialText, row, rowId, column, commit, cancel }) => node }]}
    onCellEdit={({ rowId, row, key, value, previousValue, pinned }) => updateYourData()}  // may return a Promise
    editTrigger="doubleClick"   // default; "click" opens on one click

Opens on double click (or click), Enter, F2, or typing a printable character (seeds the editor with it;
Backspace/Delete open it empty). Enter, Tab and blur commit; Tab/Shift+Tab commit and open the
next/previous editable cell across rows; Escape cancels and stops there (does not clear selection or
close a dialog). The table never mutates data: it calls onCellEdit and shows what the data says.
A returned Promise shows the new value with data-pending/aria-busy until it settles; on rejection
the cell shows the data's value again with data-failed and the error message as title. An unchanged
value reports nothing. Editors by type: text box (text and most types); number box (number, percent,
currency; step from formatOptions.decimals; currencyInMinorUnits edited in major units, returned in
minor); filterable ARIA combobox for any column with formatOptions.options, and Yes/No for boolean
(first choice clears); native date (returns "YYYY-MM-DD" for a calendar day), datetime-local (in
format.timeZone, returns the instant in the previous value's shape: ISO string, Date or epoch), time
(keeps seconds if present); tags as comma-separated words → array; json/image/file/address have
none unless renderEditor. Values come back in the shape they replaced. parse runs before validate;
validate returning a string/false keeps the editor open, aria-invalid, with the message beside it
(role=alert); blur with an invalid value abandons the edit. Popups (list, error) render outside the
table and flip above near the bottom of the window. Custom editors render in the cell and handle
their own keys; call commit(value)/cancel(). Server render has no editor open. Works in server mode.
Vue: onCellEdit is a prop (@cell-edit), renderEditor may return a VNode. In code: isCellEditable,
editorKind, editorOptions, toEditorText, fromEditorText, validateEdit, editValuesEqual, placePopup.

## Slots

toolbar · appendRow · footer · emptyState — React nodes in React; `#toolbar` `#appendRow` `#footer`
`#empty` slots in Vue; a DOM node or string in Svelte and plain JavaScript.

## Pagination

pagination={{ mode: "pages" | "simple" | "loadMore" | "infinite", pageSize, pageSizeOptions, siblings }}
pagination={false} shows every row. Changing anything that affects matching rows resets to page 1.

## State

One serialisable object:

    { sort: [{key, direction}], filters: [{key, operator, value}], match: "all"|"any", search,
      page /* 1-based */, pageSize, selection: string[], order: string[], hidden: string[],
      widths: Record<string, number>, pinned: Record<string, "start"|"end">, density,
      expanded /* row ids with an open detail */, collapsed /* parents with folded children */,
      focus /* active cell: { rowId, key?, align? } | null */ }

Keys added since 0.3.0 (expanded, collapsed, focus) are optional in the TableState type; the table
fills them in ([], [] and null).

Controlled with `state` + `onStateChange`; uncontrolled with `defaultState`. A controlled `state`
controls exactly the keys it has.
URL: stateToQueryString(state, { prefix?, include? }) and stateFromUrl(searchParams). When the URL is
the source of truth pass state={pickUrlState(state)}: the URL does not carry selection or widths, and
controlling them from it pins them to their defaults.
Saved views are JSON.stringify(state).

## Server-side data

    <Table data={page} total={total} server onStateChange={(state) => refetch(state)} />

In server mode nothing is filtered, sorted or paged by the table; `total` drives pagination.

Two things the table cannot work out from one page — the values behind a set filter and the rows
behind an export — are declared once by passing an object instead of `true`:

    <Table
      data={page}
      total={total}
      server={{
        distinct: (columnKey, state) => api.rows.distinct(columnKey),  // string[] or SelectOption[]
        all: (state) => api.rows.all(state),                           // every matching row
      }}
      export
      onStateChange={(state) => refetch(state)}
    />

`distinct` is called once per column, the first time its filter panel is opened, and remembered.
`all` is called when the user exports. A column's own `filter: { kind: "set", options }` overrules
`distinct`, and `export: { fetchRows }` overrules `all`. Both members are optional.

## Server rendering

Renders completely on a server with the correct rows in the markup, no effects and no layout shift —
in every adapter: Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, React Router, Astro islands, and plain JavaScript via
renderToString(options) from @trapezium/vanilla. In Vue, Svelte and plain JS the live table replaces
the server markup on mount (same bytes) and keeps anything done to it first — a box ticked, a
search typed. Formatting defaults (locale "en", timeZone "UTC") are fixed rather than read from
the runtime, so a server and a browser produce the same string. With `buildHref` (every adapter),
controls render as links and the table works with no client JavaScript; `linkComponent` is React only.
A multi-level sort or a header search already in the URL is rendered by the server (levels numbered,
reset link present, rows narrowed). Making one needs the script. A shift-click on a header link goes
to onNavigate with the URL of the added level when there is one, else to onStateChange, else the
browser navigates to it; the search box reports through onStateChange.
When the URL is the source of truth: state={pickUrlState(stateFromUrl(query, opts))},
buildHref={(next) => applyStateToUrl(path, next, opts)}, with opts = { defaults: { pageSize } } if the
table's page size is not 25.

## Styling

CSS custom properties on `.tpz` (--tpz-surface, --tpz-muted, --tpz-border, --tpz-primary,
--tpz-row-height, --tpz-header-height, --tpz-font-mono, …), and --tpz-cell-content-height on each
cell (see Cell renderers). Dark mode follows the page's color-scheme, or `.dark` /
[data-theme="dark"] on an ancestor, or theme="dark" on the table.
classNames={{ root, frame, toolbar, search, scroll, table, thead, tbody, headerRow, headerCell, row,
cell, selectCell, dragCell, expandCell, detailRow, detailCell, pagination, empty, footer }} adds classes;
`unstyled` drops the defaults. Same in
every adapter.
responsive="cards" stacks rows below 40rem of container width, in pure CSS.
Bridge to shadcn/ui: import "@trapezium/react/themes/shadcn.css" when the app's tokens are whole
colours (oklch(...), hsl(...)), or "@trapezium/react/themes/shadcn-hsl.css" when they are bare HSL
channels like `--background: 210 20% 98%`, which is the Tailwind 3 convention. Picking the wrong one
leaves every colour unset.

## Headless

`useTable(props)` returns { rows, rowIds, total, pageCount, filtered, columns, hiddenColumns,
allColumns, state, update, patch, types, format, pagination, selection, server,
headerSearchDebounce }.
`@trapezium/core` has the whole engine with no renderer.

## Not included, on purpose

Grouping, aggregation, pivoting, multi-level tree data, formulas, Excel export.

## Migrating from AG Grid

columnDefs→columns · field→key · headerName→header · valueGetter→key with a dotted path, or
accessor(row) · valueFormatter→format(ctx) · cellRenderer→render(ctx) · cellClass→className ·
pinned:"left"→pin:"start" · filter:"agSetColumnFilter"→filter:"set" ·
filter:"agNumberColumnFilter"→filter:"range" · filter:"agDateColumnFilter"→filter:"date" ·
rowSelection:"multiple"→selection · quickFilterText→search prop or state.search ·
floatingFilter:true→headerSearch · multiSortKey/suppressMultiSort→sortable={{ multiple }} ·
getRowStyle/getRowClass→rowClassName(row, index) · onRowClicked→onRowClick (clicks on links,
buttons and inputs inside a row are already ignored) · rowHeight→rowHeight · getRowHeight→
rowHeight:"auto" (the browser measures it; there is nothing to answer) · autoHeight→wrap:true ·
wrapText→wrap · domLayout→maxHeight · flex→grow · headerTooltip→description ·
headerComponent→renderHeader (text) / renderHeaderControls (inputs, buttons) · masterDetail/detailCellRenderer/isRowMaster→detail={{ render, canExpand }} ·
editable/cellEditor/valueParser→editable/renderEditor/parse · onCellValueChanged→onCellEdit ·
singleClickEdit→editTrigger="click" · ensureIndexVisible/setFocusedCell→focusCell(state, rowId, key) ·
treeData (one level)→getParentId · pinnedTopRowData/pinnedBottomRowData→pinnedRows={{ top, bottom }} ·
rowDragManaged/onRowDragEnd→rowReorder={{ onReorder }} · getContextMenuItems→onRowContextMenu ·
serverSideDatasource→server={{ distinct, all }} with onStateChange · exportDataAsCsv→export ·
ModuleRegistry.registerModules→nothing.

A per-column `comparator` usually wants to be a custom type instead: defineType once and every
column of that type sorts, filters, formats and exports consistently. There is no grid API object
and no ref to call methods on — everything is state, and `onStateChange` reports it.
